why: I checked all seven verifier checks against the words of their expect lines. Checks 1–5 require stdout to be "exactly" the expected JSON plus a newline, and check 1 also requires exit 0. That is what the expect lines say "prints exactly … followed by a newline" means, so it adds nothing extra. In check 3, "rows in a different order" follows from "in order" and "exactly". Check 6 passes on "exit=0" plus a test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-containing input and asserts on the output, which matches its expect line. Check 7 needs only a mention of --tsv and an example invocation that uses it. The stricter points are all under "Advisory": the proof's "say that the flag means tab-separated input", the test:cli script, the non-goals and testing the flag at different argument positions. Nothing stricter appears in any PASS or FAIL condition.
